item.title: Experimental investigation and modeling of ductile fracture in steel at low temperatures

item.title: Angle-dependent shielding performance of Ti-6Al-4V/AISI 1045 bilayer panel under hypervelocity impact
item.description: 库内相似论文：An experimental and numerical investigation on enhancing the ballistic resistance of 316L stainless steel plates against blunt projectiles by covering with 2024-T351 aluminum alloy thin plates（相似度 0.731） 塑性变形与硬化律: 可作为硬化律选型与颈缩后外推方案的参考（规则推断，非已验证迁移） 迁移前检查: 核对标定应变范围、外推是否有独立验证、是否混用不同试样 摘要片段: Results demonstrated that impact angle, after … 标题/摘要不能确认全部实验条件与方法适用性，未陈述内容保持未知 用户子程序与数值实现: 可作为显式积分算法、正则化方案与子程序实现细节的参考（规则推断，非已验证迁移） 迁移前检查: 核对单元类型与尺寸、耗散能、稳定性与网格收敛性 摘要片段: Using the Modified Johnson–Cook material model … 标题/摘要不能确认全部实验条件与方法适用性，未陈述内容保持未知 摘要方法线索: Johnson-Cook https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Angle-dependent+shielding+performance+of+Ti-6Al-4V%2FAISI+1045+bilayer+panel+under+hypervelo&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1177%2F10567895261500988%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22plasticity_hardening%22%2C+%22umat_implementation%22%2C+%22impact_validation%22%2C+%22other_metals%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Hypervelocity ballistic impacts are becoming common with scientific advancements in propulsion technology. Space collisions like meteoroids also involve high-velocity impacts. Traditional metallic sheets like Ti-6Al-4V and AISI 1045 steel, when employed in thin configurations, exhibit limited capacity to endure the severe stresses generated during high-speed impact events. In this paper, the response of a Ti-6Al-4V titanium alloy and AISI 1045 steel bilayer panel to a hypervelocity aluminum ball impact was studied to observe the underlying phenomenon of spalling, cavitation, and debris-cloud formation caused by such hypervelocity impacts. Using the Modified Johnson–Cook material model along with the Grüneisen equation of state to represent the impacted materials and implementing the smoothed particle hydrodynamics approach within the commercially available finite-element software LS-DYNA, the penetration behavior under symmetric and asymmetric impact conditions was investigated. Results demonstrated that impact angle, after the critical threshold of 30°, strongly influenced the energy distribution, flow stress, and the rear-face bulge formation of the lower AISI 1045 steel plate. These findings provide practical design guidance for optimizing multi-layer metallic shielding and impact-resistant structures against hypervelocity debris. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+A+High-Temperature+Semi-Coupled+Damage+Model+for+7075+Aluminum+Alloy+Considering+Temperatu&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.3390%2Fma19214650%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22temperature%22%2C+%22strain_rate%22%2C+%22damage_evolution%22%2C+%22calibration%22%2C+%22other_metals%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Fracture is a common and fatal defect in the hot stamping of aluminum alloys. Accurate prediction of high-temperature fracture behavior is crucial for forming process planning. However, existing high-temperature fracture criteria suffer from a trade-off between predictive capability and parameter calibration difficulty, which limits their industrial application. This study establishes a high-temperature semi-coupled damage model by incorporating strain rate and temperature terms into a semi-coupled fracture framework and coupling it with a viscoplastic constitutive model. This model maintains the convenience of parameter calibration while describing the nonlinear characteristics of damage evolution using a hyperbolic sine function. The model was applied to the finite element analysis of 7075 aluminum alloy. For hot tensile tests, the simulated load–displacement responses, fracture displacements, and strain fields agree with the experiments, with a maximum load–displacement root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.047 kN and a maximum fracture displacement relative error of 3.141%. For isothermal bulging validation tests, the average relative error for fracture location prediction is 5.10%, and the maximum relative error for normalized thickness is 6.67%. These results demonstrate that within 350–450 °C and 0.001–0.1 s−1, the proposed model accurately predicts the damage initiation, evolution, and fracture behavior. item.title: Prediction of fracture behavior in cold roll-bonded multilayer metallic composite sheets using ductile fracture criteria
item.category: Journal of Materials Research and Technology
item.description: 库内相似论文：Fracture prediction for metal sheet deformation under different stress states with uncoupled ductile fracture criteria（相似度 0.748） 与《Micromechanically-motivated phenomenological Hosford–Coulomb model for predicting ductile fracture initiation at low stress triaxialities》共享 2 篇参考文献；归一化重合度 0.033 共享参考文献示例：https://openalex.org/W2000595666, https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Prediction+of+fracture+behavior+in+cold+roll-bonded+multilayer+metallic+composite+sheets+u&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1016%2Fj.jmrt.2026.10.268%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22stress_state%22%2C+%22ductile_fracture%22%2C+%22damage_evolution%22%2C+%22other_metals%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 In this study, the fracture behavior of CRB Al/Cu multilayer sheets was investigated using six uncoupled ductile fracture criteria including Ayada, Rice–Tracy, Brozzo, Oh, Oyane–Sato, and Ko–Huh. Five different materials were examined, including pure aluminum (AA1050), pure copper, Al/Al bilayer, Al/Cu bilayer, and Cu/Al/Cu trilayer composites. The calibration of the fracture models was performed using a hybrid approach (experimental tests, theoretical analysis and numerical simulation), and subsequently validated through independent plane-strain tensile tests. The results show that the predictive capability of uncoupled fracture criteria is strongly material-dependent. The Brozzo criterion provides the highest accuracy for the Al/Al bilayer (1.6% error), the Oh criterion performs best for the Al/Cu bilayer (0.1% error), and the Ko–Huh criterion gives the closest prediction for the Cu/Al/Cu trilayer (1.8% error). A comparison of the calibrated fracture loci further reveals that prediction accuracy is governed by the compatibility between the stress-state sensitivity of the fracture criterion and the damage evolution of the multilayer architecture, rather than by the intrinsic superiority of any individual model. These findings demonstrate that no single fracture criterion is universally applicable to CRB multilayer sheets. Nevertheless, the Ko–Huh and Oyane–Sato criteria exhibited relatively consistent performance across the investigated multilayer configurations, indicating that they can be considered suitable candidates for fracture prediction of the investigated multilayer sheets within the stress-state range examined in this study. Chemical short-range order (SRO) can markedly affect the mechanical response of high-entropy alloys (HEAs), but its role in void-containing alloys under high-strain-rate loading remains unclear. Here, molecular dynamics simulations and a data-driven surrogate model were combined to investigate the tensile response of Al 0.3 FeCoCrNi HEAs with pre-existing nanoscale voids. The results reveal a coupling effect between structural defects and local chemical ordering. The size of pre-existing voids dominates yield onset, peak strength and damage evolution by intensifying stress concentration and promoting earlier plasticity. By contrast, SRO acts as a conditional atomic-scale modifier. For smaller voids, SRO improves tensile resistance by reducing active dislocation nucleation sites, confining early plastic zones, and promoting sessile reactions including Lomer-Cottrell locks and Hirth dislocations. This effect becomes less pronounced for larger voids, where deformation is increasingly governed by void-induced stress concentration. Temperature further constrains the SRO effect: SRO promotes twinning and organized planar-defect evolution at 300 K, whereas thermal activation suppresses twinning and causes diffuse post-yield defect accumulation at 1200 K. The proposed surrogate model provides an efficient mapping of the stress response and damage evolution across the studied parameter space. These findings identify SRO as a conditional design parameter for tuning defect tolerance in HEAs. Published: 2026-11-01T00:00:00+00:00 Venue: Materials & Design 研究类型: 跨金属方法参考

https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+A+hybrid+model%E2%80%93data+framework+for+elastoplasticity+with+kinematic+and+isotropic+hardening&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1007%2Fs00466-026-02878-4%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22stress_state%22%2C+%22plasticity_hardening%22%2C+%22umat_implementation%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Abstract Data-driven computational mechanics offers an alternative solution methodology to conventional methods by replacing constitutive models with data spaces defining admissible material states. Originally proposed for linear elasticity, its application to plasticity remains challenging. Purely data-driven plasticity schemes are usually restricted to one-dimensional problems due to the excessively large data space required as a result of path dependence. Hybrid frameworks combining constitutive assumptions with data have shown promise but are often limited by their underlying assumptions such as isotropic hardening or their inability to capture strain-path changes. In this work, a new hybrid model–data plasticity framework is proposed that incorporates kinematic and isotropic hardening via data spaces derived from discrete datasets, while adopting Prager’s law for back stress evolution without explicitly defining its functional form. The approach preserves the standard computational plasticity algorithmic procedures, while an implicit return-mapping procedure and a search direction calculation akin to the elastoplastic tangent are performed through the data spaces. Numerical examples in one and three-dimensional problems demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in more general plasticity problems. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Recurrent+neural+network+constitutive+model+for+human+rib+cortical+bone+and+its+biological&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1016%2Fj.cma.2026.119532%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22umat_implementation%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Integrating the biological variability of human rib cortical bone into constitutive models is of interest to quantify the uncertainty of the biomechanical response at population level, e.g., in virtual automotive crash assessments, yet current constitutive models typically rely on fixed material properties. Because biological tissues are complex to model, this work proposes an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) ansatz to tackle this difficulty. The model comprises a recurrent neural network based on the extended Minimal State Cell (MSC) for elastoplasticity, augmented with transfer learning (TL) layers that account for the biological variability by modulating the input and output of the MSC. It was trained on stress–strain time series under non-monotonic multiaxial plane stress conditions for discrete values of the variability parameter and learned a smooth mapping over it, enabling interpolation to intermediate values without retraining. Self-consistency allowed training on short sequences ( ∼ 1 0 2 steps) while evaluating accurately on very long sequences ( ∼ 1 0 6 steps), as needed for online predictions inside the FEM scheme. The ANN model was deployed in a commercial explicit solver through a vectorized user material subroutine (UMAT). Moreover, a novel intrusive stochastic method is proposed in which the variability parameter follows a probability distribution within the material subroutine, propagating material uncertainty without multiple runs or solver modifications. The method allows for the estimation of the distributions of stresses and boundary forces within a single simulation. On a coupon geometry, the ANN remained stable over ∼ 1 0 6 time steps in both deterministic and stochastic simulations with uniform, normal, and bimodal distributions. ABSTRACT This contribution presents a phasefield approach to simulating combined brittle and ductile fracture in a materially heterogeneous domain consisting of a ductile 100Cr6 steel matrix and various non‐metallic, brittle inclusions. The matrix subdomain is modeled with von Mises plasticity with linear isotropic hardening, while the inclusions are assumed to stay in the linear elastic range. Plane strain and 3D simulations of uni‐axial tension and contact loading show the brittle inclusion subdomains as preferred loci for crack nucleation, in qualitative agreement with experimental data for cyclically loaded industrial bearings. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Aspects+of+mesh+sensitivity+for+phenomenological+damage+models+using+small+solid+and+large&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1016%2Fj.mtcomm.2026.116533%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22umat_implementation%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Application-oriented simulations, such as automotive crash simulations, often utilize large shell elements to optimize computational efficiency. This study applies the crack band approach typically used for concrete materials to steel sheets. The aim was to examine this regularization method for different stress states with plane stress shell elements to reduce mesh sensitivity, in respect to element size as well as to element shape. Finite element simulations of four specimens covering the lower and mid triaxiality range were performed with LS-Dyna using small solid elements and large shell elements. For each specimen, the results of a finite element simulation performed with large shell elements were compared with results of a block of solid elements of equal dimensions. Each finite element solver uses different shell formulations, which can influence the exact results of the simulation. Nonetheless, the comparison provides insights into the expected behavior compared to the behavior resulting from shell simulations. The guidelines developed in this study were tested numerically for a tensile test with a spot weld by comparing differently discretized meshes. The results show that the characteristic length determined by the crack band approach improves shell element simulations compared to the conventionally calculated characteristic length. This approach accommodates various aspect ratios and arbitrarily shaped shell elements. Accurate numerical reproduction of Charpy impact tests requires constitutive and damage models capable of representing material behavior under dynamic loading conditions. This study presents an experimental–numerical investigation of the impact response of sub-size AISI 304 stainless-steel Charpy specimens characterized by different thicknesses and notch depths. Instrumented tests were performed using a 50 J pendulum impact system at an impact velocity of 3.458 m/s. The experimental force, displacement, velocity, and absorbed-energy histories were used as reference data for explicit finite element simulations developed in LS-DYNA using the Johnson–Cook constitutive and damage model. A two-level full factorial Design of Experiments, comprising 64 simulations, was conducted by varying six Johnson–Cook parameters—A, B, n, D1, D2, and D3—by ±20% relative to their baseline values. The effects of these parameters on the peak impact force were evaluated using a General Linear Model and the Analysis of Variance. Then, the sensitivity results were used to guide the calibration of the most influential parameters, and the resulting parameter set was assessed across the different specimen geometries. Overall, the calibrated model reproduced the initial loading stage, peak-force magnitude, and energy-absorption trends with reasonable accuracy. The largest discrepancies occurred during the post-peak and fracture stages, including differences between the experimentally observed and numerically predicted fracture conditions. The results demonstrate that DOE-guided sensitivity analysis can reduce parameter space and support a more systematic calibration process. However, they also show that calibration based primarily on peak force is insufficient to ensure an accurate prediction of post-peak behavior and fracture conditions across different sub-size specimen geometries. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+A+Hybrid+Shallow%E2%80%93Deep+Neural+Network-Based+Constitutive+Model+for+High-Temperature+Flow+St&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.3390%2Fmet16111198%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22temperature%22%2C+%22plasticity_hardening%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Ti-6Al-4V titanium alloy is widely used in aerospace, space exploration, and automotive manufacturing. Characterizing its high-temperature flow stress is essential for engineering design and numerical simulation. To address the limited prediction accuracy of the conventional Johnson–Cook constitutive model and the generalization challenges of neural networks trained on small datasets, this study develops a hybrid shallow–deep neural network workflow. Mechanical tests at 25, 100, 150, 200, and 300 °C characterize the constitutive behavior and fracture features of large Ti-6Al-4V castings. A shallow neural network learns the response within the sampled domain, while a long short-term memory (LSTM) network extends temperature-dependent stress predictions beyond this domain. The generated data support subsequent nonlinear regression to determine the parameters of a modified Johnson–Cook constitutive model, which is compared with the available experimental responses. The workflow is further incorporated into a project-based engineering mathematics software course using the Deep Learning Toolbox in MATLAB R2021a. Through experimental data processing, constitutive fitting, neural-network-assisted data generation, subinterval error evaluation, and failure diagnosis, the instructional case develops students’ capabilities in data-driven modeling, reproducible computation, and cautious extrapolation. Published: 2026-10-29T00:00:00+00:00 Venue: Metals 研究类型: TC4核心研究

https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Impact+of+TiC+particle+size+and+concentration+on+the+microstructure+and+mechanical+propert&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1016%2Fj.msea.2026.151337%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22other_metals%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF) enables the fabrication of lightweight aluminum components, but processing Al–Cu alloys remains challenging due to their wide solidification interval and susceptibility to solidification cracking associated with columnar grain growth. Grain refinement via inoculant addition is effective, but most reported strategies rely on nanoparticles, which tend to agglomerate and raise health and handling concerns. Consequently, coarser ceramic particles have emerged as safer alternatives. This study investigates the effects of TiC particle size (45 nm, 4 μm, and 44 μm) and concentration (1, 2, and 4 wt.%) on the microstructure and mechanical properties of AA2017 alloy processed by L-PBF. The results show that grain refinement and columnar-to-equiaxed transition (CET) arise from the combined effects of heterogeneous nucleation on TiC and in situ–formed L1 2 -Al 3 Ti particles, together with solute-induced constitutional supercooling and growth restriction effects. TiC particle size critically governs refinement efficiency: although nanoparticles exhibit high nucleation potential, agglomeration limits their effectiveness, whereas coarse particles show reduced reactivity and insufficient Ti release. Fine micrometer-sized TiC particles (4 μm) provide an optimal balance between surface area and dispersion. Adding 2 wt.% TiC (4 μm) enables effective CET and grain refinement while providing a favorable strength–ductility balance (ultimate tensile strength of 372 ± 1 MPa and elongation of 18 ± 5%), whereas 4 wt.% TiC (4 μm) provides higher strength but lower elongation. Overall, fine micrometer-sized TiC particles therefore represent an effective and safe alternative to nanoparticles for additive manufacturing of aluminum alloys. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Cyclic+Deformation+Characteristics+of+Laser-Cladding+Additively+Manufactured+316L+Stainles&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1061%2Fjsendh.steng-15279%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22plasticity_hardening%22%2C+%22calibration%22%2C+%22other_metals%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Abstract Laser cladding (LC) is a 3D printing technology that has been increasingly applied to the repair and strengthening of civil engineering structures. However, research on the cyclic performance of laser-clad materials is currently limited. Therefore, 11 specimens were fabricated using LC technology, and experiments were conducted to investigate the mechanical properties and hysteretic behavior of the LC material under different cyclic loading protocols. The experimental results show that laser-clad 316L stainless steel has excellent energy dissipation capacity. LC 316L stainless steel subjected to cyclic loading demonstrates mixed hardening behavior, including isotropic hardening and kinematic hardening, along with a pronounced Bauschinger effect. The envelope curve of 316L stainless steel under cyclic loading differs from its monotonic tensile curve, with the Ramberg–Osgood model proving effective in characterizing the envelope behavior. The elastic modulus of 316L stainless steel initially decreases during the first few loading cycles before stabilizing with accumulated plastic strain. The Chaboche model was implemented to predict the stress–strain response of LC 316L stainless steel, with parameter calibration and subsequent validation confirming the predictive accuracy of the model. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Bead-resolved+prediction+of+warpage%2C+residual+stress%2C+and+high-stress+locations+in+metal-f&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1080%2F17452759.2026.2753957%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22umat_implementation%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Green metal-filled PLA parts are fragile in the as-printed state, and part-scale simulation tools cannot resolve where bead-level stresses concentrate. We present a bead-resolved thermo-viscoelastic eigenstrain framework that ingests a pre-computed thermal history and predicts the as-printed geometry, residual stress field, and highest-stress locations of green metal-PLA parts. The solver chain is validated against the ABS planar-spring benchmark of Cattenone et al., reproducing the eleven-probe experimental mean to −5.2% with a lower normalised RMSE (20.7% vs 23.5% of the experimental mean) than the benchmark’s Abaqus simulation, with two quantities calibrated to the benchmark and no rescaling. Predicted geometry matches 3D scans of IN718-PLA and Cu-PLA specimens to 0.07–0.10 mm typical lateral and 0.04–0.09 mm vertical deviation, measured against six separately fabricated specimens per material. A three-case sequential-isolation design recovers the closed-form cross-material stress ratio σ_Cu/σ_IN = (E_Cu/E_IN)·(α_Cu/α_IN), with α the along-raster contraction coefficient, to within 6% and verifies numerically that displacement is decoupled from modulus: a 2.2× modulus change alters the predicted geometry by under 0.002 mm. The bead-level map of elastic stress demand is robust to joint constitutive perturbation (ρ ≥ 0.98), and 195 of the top 200 highest-stress beads coincide between materials, which motivates single-simulation feedstock screening. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+On+the+Extraction+of+Elastic%E2%80%93Plastic+Constitutive+Properties+From+Three-Dimensional+Deform&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1115%2F1.4030322%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22stress_state%22%2C+%22calibration%22%2C+%22other_metals%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 In this article, a coupled experimental and numerical method is utilized for characterizing the elastic–plastic constitutive properties of ductile materials. Three-dimensional digital image correlation (DIC) is used to measure the full field deformation on two mutually orthogonal surfaces of a uniaxial tensile test specimen. The material’s constitutive model, whose parameters are unknown a priori, is determined through an optimization process that compares these experimental measurements with finite element simulations in which the constitutive model is implemented. The optimization procedure utilizes the robust dataset of locally observed deformation measurements from DIC in addition to the standard measurements of boundary load and displacement data. When the difference between the experiment and simulations is reduced sufficiently, a set of parameters is found for the material model that is suitable to large strain levels. This method of material characterization is applied to a tensile specimen fabricated from a sheet of 15-5 PH stainless steel. This method proves to be a powerful tool for calibration of material models. The final parameters produce a simulation that tracks the local experimental displacement field to within a couple percent of error. Simultaneously, the percent error in the simulation for the load carried by the specimen throughout the test is less than 1%. Additionally, half of the parameters for Hill’s yield criterion, describing anisotropy of the normal stresses, are found from a single tensile test. This method will find even greater utility in calibrating more complex material models by greatly reducing the experimental effort required to identify the appropriate model parameters. item.title: High-velocity perforation of medium-entropy CrCoNi thin plates by spherical projectiles
item.category: 跨圈方法发现（非近期新作）
item.description: 跨圈方法发现（非近期新作） 库内相似论文：Experimental-numerical study on ballistic impact behavior of 316L austenitic stainless steel plates against blunt and ogival projectiles（相似度 0.863） 与《Plasticity, ductile fracture and ballistic impact behavior of Ti-6Al-4V Alloy》共享 3 篇参考文献；归一化重合度 0.049 共享参考文献示例：https://openalex.org/W2036336844, https://openalex.org/W2086827153, https://openalex.org/W3042024306 冲击侵彻与模型验证: 可作为从材料试样走向结构尺度验证的线索（规则推断，非已验证迁移） 迁移前检查: 核对弹靶几何、边界条件、速度区间、残余速度与失效形貌是否同时对上 仅题名片段: High-velocity perforation of medium-entropy CrCoNi thin … 标题/摘要不能确认全部实验条件与方法适用性，未陈述内容保持未知 公开阅读反馈 直接有用:
